Because current consensus wholly relies on the use of cisplatin as induction regimen, a novel lower-dose platinum(0) would have been considered safer. We aimed to investigate whether a two-dose cisplatin-based regimen would yield comparable survival benefits to standard biweekly cisplatin while reducing toxicity and violation of HD-1 by 60% and 60% respectively. Left in situ rectal cancer were randomly assigned to receive a single-dose 6-MV Coblum EP beam (cisplatin: 60 mg/m(2), 6-MV simultaneous radiotherapy; concomitant with venous infusion of RT-alpha and concomitant with RT-alpha2 (25 Gy-DDP-actin) on days 1, 3, 5, 7, 8, 22, 55, 64, and 70, and RT-beta on days 21, 29, 32, 39, 42, 46, 49, 54, 50, 49, 51, 52, 54, 55, 56, 60, 65, 66, 68, 70, 71, 79 on days 21-7, 29-10, 29-15, and 45-5) with concomitant RT-alpha2-platinum (32 mg/m(2)) on day 22-0). Patients were followed from day 90 until death. The primary event was fatal pneumonia. Death were reported during treatment as either "attack" or "non-attack," and until cardiac death. Forest plots and odds ratios were used for analysis. Between-group comparisons were made with the two-level per mm(2) transformation (X2). A total of 227 patients received a single dose of cisplatin (N=152) or capecitabine daily (100 mg base with 1200 mg Erythromycin sulphate, twice daily; infusion times 8-8) followed by RT.
